Foundation Identifies Over 23,000 Phishing Email Attempts in Passport Wallet Security Incident

Passport hardware wallet maker Foundation said it has identified more than 23,000 phishing email attempts, including 19,057 messages delivered through Mailgun and 1,503 sent via Google Workspace. The number of affected users remains unknown.

The investigation found that personal information from historical WooCommerce orders remained in legacy database tables despite appearing redacted in the admin dashboard. Customer data from orders placed through Shopify since May may also have been exposed. Foundation said it has revoked affected email credentials and taken compromised legacy services offline. There is no evidence that Passport devices or their private keys were compromised. The phishing emails attempted to trick users into revealing their wallet recovery phrases. — link

Zcash Co-Founder Proposes Redirecting 8% of Block Subsidies to Network Sustainability Mechanism

Zcash co-founder and protocol developer Sean Bowe has submitted a draft Zcash Improvement Proposal (ZIP) to end the 8% block subsidy allocation to Zcash Community Grants (ZCG) and redirect it to the Network Sustainability Mechanism (NSM), withholding the funds from immediate circulation.

The proposal argues that ZCG's existing reserves are sufficient to sustain its grant-making activities. It would leave ZCG's existing treasury, the separate 12% Coinholder-Controlled Fund allocation, miners' subsidy share, and ZEC's maximum supply unchanged. — link

Binance Files for Brazilian Crypto License Ahead of October 30 Deadline; Restricts 8 Services and Delists 22 Tokens in Brazil

Binance filed an application with Brazil’s central bank on October 23 through its local entity BBrasil to operate as a virtual asset service provider (SPSAV), ahead of the October 30 regulatory deadline, according to Blocknews. To comply with local rules, Binance began restricting eight services for Brazilian users on October 27, including crypto loans, margin trading, mining pools and cloud mining, while delisting 22 tokens, including USDE, USTC, DCR and XVG. Existing positions in affected products are generally limited to reductions or closures, with new positions prohibited. Binance also plans to complete the migration of Brazilian users to its local payment-account structure by October 29. — link

Binance Says It Blocked Multiple North Korea-Linked Cyberattacks Over the Past Week, With No Asset Losses

Binance said on October 27 that its security team had successfully identified and blocked multiple North Korea-linked cyberattacks over the past week, with no damage to company systems or loss of assets. Binance noted that North Korea-linked hacking groups have continued to conduct social engineering attacks under the “Contagious Interview” campaign, using fake job interviews, coding tests, and software installation requests to trick targets into running malicious programs. The exchange advised users to avoid installing unauthorized software or executing code from untrusted sources, adding that it will continue strengthening security monitoring, threat detection, and internal security controls. — link

Coinbase to Automatically Convert 14 Restricted Crypto Assets for EEA Users on October 30

Under Coinbase's previously announced MiCA compliance measures, retail users in the European Economic Area (EEA) must withdraw 14 restricted crypto assets, including USDT, PYUSD, USD1, DAI, and PAXG, before October 30. On that date, Coinbase will automatically convert remaining balances into USDC or other supported assets or currencies at prevailing market rates.

Trading and conversions of these assets have already been restricted. Coinbase warned that deposits received after the deadline will not be credited to user accounts or included in the automatic conversion process, and recovery cannot be guaranteed. The restrictions affect assets issued by Tether, PayPal, and Trump-linked World Liberty Financial, among others. — link

Reuters: CFTC Again Probes Whether Polymarket Violated 2022 Settlement

According to Reuters, citing two sources familiar with the matter, the CFTC is investigating whether Polymarket violated its 2022 settlement by failing to take sufficient steps to block U.S. users from its offshore platform. The investigation covers Polymarket's geolocation controls and U.S. advertising activities. The agency is also examining customer onboarding and protection measures on Polymarket's U.S. platform. The CFTC and DOJ closed similar investigations in 2025 without bringing charges. Both Polymarket and the CFTC declined to comment. — link

Wallet Potentially Linked to $40M UXLINK Hack Shows $6.54M in Unrealized ETH Gains

A wallet suspected of belonging to the hacker behind last year’s roughly $40 million UXLINK theft holds a 30,282 ETH long on Hyperliquid, according to on-chain data. The position has an average entry price of $2,134.45 and is worth approximately $71.17 million, with $6.54 million in unrealized gains. A funding address associated with the position and a known UXLINK hacker address both transferred ETH held for gas fees to the same wallet on the same day. The trader began trading ETH on Hyperliquid in early August after consolidating roughly 11.55 million USDC from multiple sources, with five of six trades showing a profit. — link

Robinhood Q3 Revenue Meets Estimates as Prediction Market Revenue Surges and Crypto Revenue Falls 55%

Robinhood reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1.424 billion, up 12% year-over-year and roughly in line with the $1.42 billion estimate. Net income fell 14% to $476 million, while diluted EPS of $0.51 missed the $0.56 estimate, including $0.07 per share in unrealized losses primarily related to Robinhood Ventures Fund I. Adjusted EBITDA rose 9% to $808 million.

Prediction market event contract revenue increased more than sixfold to $173 million, while crypto transaction revenue declined 55% to $120 million. Crypto notional trading volume fell 38% to $50 billion, while event contracts traded rose more than sevenfold to 16.4 billion. Robinhood Chain recorded over $80 billion in DEX trading volume and more than $50 million in network fees during its first quarter on mainnet. The company also lowered the upper end of its 2026 adjusted operating expenses and stock-based compensation outlook from $2.775 billion to $2.75 billion, keeping the lower end at $2.675 billion. — link
